name: Marsha Blackburn
bio: Tennessee's senior U.S. senator since 2019, Blackburn is the polling frontrunner with broad establishment support and statewide name recognition. Trump-aligned conservative.

early_childhood_ed.summary: Marsha Blackburn has not taken a detailed public position on pre-K expansion or childcare programs. She supports school choice broadly through expansion of Tennessee's Education Freedom Scholarships but has not specifically addressed early childhood education or childcare costs in her gubernatorial campaign.
early_childhood_ed.details: According to TNFirefly's 2026 race tracker, Blackburn has 'No Public Position' on Pre-K and early childhood education. Her education platform centers on strongly expanding the Education Freedom Scholarship (EFS) program for K-12 school choice and dissolving the U.S. Department of Education. In a 2026 Knox News voter questionnaire, she stated she will 'always fight to make certain that every child gets the education they deserve' but made no mention of childcare, pre-K, or early learning programs. She has emphasized workforce development via TCAT expansion.

child_hunger.summary: As a U.S. Senator, Blackburn co-sponsored the 'Keep SNAP Funded Act' in October 2025 to ensure SNAP benefits continued during the government shutdown, citing that roughly 690,000 Tennesseans depend on the program. She also voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which cut $186 billion from SNAP nationally.
child_hunger.details: In October 2025, Senator Blackburn co-sponsored legislation to fund SNAP during the government shutdown, stating: 'Roughly one in 10 Tennesseans receive SNAP benefits for food assistance, and they shouldn't have to worry about where their next meal will come from because the Democrats are holding government funding hostage.' However, Blackburn also voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (H.R. 1), which cut $186 billion from SNAP nationally beginning July 2025 and added expanded work requirements. As of June 2026, approximately 100,000 Tennesseans had lost SNAP benefits since those changes took effect. No specific campaign-trail statements on child hunger as governor candidate were found.

parental_support.summary: Blackburn's campaign platform emphasizes expanding school choice for parents through Education Freedom Scholarships and parental rights in education. She has not publicly addressed paid family leave, childcare subsidies, or the Child Tax Credit as part of her gubernatorial campaign.
parental_support.details: Blackburn's campaign questionnaire responses frame parental support primarily through school choice and parental rights in education. She states: 'Parents know what's best for their children — not the government. School choice empowers parents to do what is right for their kids by giving them options.' She pledges to expand Education Freedom Scholarships to all families. She emphasizes public safety for children as a top gubernatorial priority. No specific positions on paid family leave, childcare subsidies, the Child Tax Credit, or direct economic support for families with young children were found.

name: John Rose
bio: Four-term congressman from the Cumberland Plateau leaving his House seat to run. Farmer and small-business owner from Cookeville.
photo_credit: U.S. House Office of the Clerk

early_childhood_ed.summary: John Rose has not taken a detailed public position on pre-K expansion or childcare programs. According to the TNFirefly race tracker, he has 'No Public Position' on Pre-K. His education platform centers on improving K-12 public school outcomes and supporting school choice.
early_childhood_ed.details: According to TNFirefly's 2026 race tracker, Rose has 'No Public Position' on Pre-K and early childhood education. His education platform focuses on K-12 improvements: appointing an Education Commissioner with Tennessee public school teaching experience, supporting the Education Freedom Scholarship program, promoting local control, and dissolving the U.S. Department of Education. He states: 'The son of a public school teacher, education is a high priority' and 90% of students will go through public schools. He pledged to 'support vulnerable children by improving the Department of Children's Services' and make Tennessee 'a national leader when it comes to making adoption attainable for Tennessee families.' No specific statements on pre-K, Head Start, childcare costs, or childcare tax credits were found.

child_hunger.summary: No public position on child hunger, SNAP, or food insecurity programs was found specifically for John Rose's gubernatorial campaign. He voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which cut federal SNAP funding and tightened work requirements.
child_hunger.details: John Rose voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (H.R. 1) in Congress, which cut $186 billion from SNAP nationally starting July 2025 and expanded work and school enrollment requirements for recipients. As of June 2026, approximately 100,000 Tennesseans had lost SNAP benefits. His campaign website and questionnaire responses do not address SNAP, child hunger, food banks, school meals, WIC, or related programs. No direct campaign-trail statements on child hunger or food insecurity as governor candidate were found as of July 2026.

parental_support.summary: Rose emphasizes parental choice in education and protecting children from 'woke indoctrination,' pledging to protect children from gender transition treatments. His campaign has not addressed paid family leave, childcare subsidies, or direct economic support for families with young children.
parental_support.details: Rose's campaign platform states: 'Parents must have a seat at the table. Parents know what is best for their children and their families. Let's give parents freedom to choose what works best for their family, whether that be in a public school, homeschool, public charter school, or private school.' Under 'Protect Tennessee Kids and Families,' he opposes gender-affirming care for minors and pledges to defend children from 'woke indoctrination.' He voted for the PROTECT Kids Act (H.R. 2616), requiring parental consent before schools change a student's gender markers. Rose pledged to make Tennessee 'a national leader when it comes to making adoption attainable for Tennessee families.' No positions on paid family leave, childcare subsidies, the Child Tax Credit, or maternal health programs were found.

name: Monty Fritts
bio: East Tennessee state legislator running on a populist conservative platform. Lower profile statewide than Blackburn or Rose.
photo_credit: No headshot found at direct image URL; visit campaign site

early_childhood_ed.summary: Monty Fritts has not taken a public position on pre-K or childcare expansion. His education platform focuses on opposing the Education Freedom Scholarship voucher program as unconstitutional and returning education to constitutional fundamentals. TNFirefly lists him as having 'No Public Position' on Pre-K.
early_childhood_ed.details: According to TNFirefly's race tracker, Fritts has 'No Public Position' on Pre-K and early childhood education. He is the only Republican gubernatorial candidate to oppose the Education Freedom Scholarship program, calling it 'fiscally irresponsible' and 'unconstitutional.' His campaign platform states under 'Save Education, Respect Parents': 'Put reading, writing, math, and civics ahead of ideology' and 'Parents are the first and final voice in their children's education.' He was the only lawmaker to vote against continuing the Tennessee Department of Education at a 2025 sunset hearing. No statements on early childhood education or childcare costs were found in his campaign materials.

child_hunger.summary: No public position on child hunger, SNAP, food insecurity, or nutrition programs was found for Monty Fritts. His platform focuses on cutting state spending and eliminating the 4% grocery sales tax as a cost-of-living measure.
child_hunger.details: No public statements from Monty Fritts on child hunger, SNAP, WIC, school meals, food banks, or food insecurity were found in his campaign materials or news coverage as of July 2026. His campaign platform includes eliminating the 4% grocery sales tax as a signature populist issue — 'Eliminate the 4% grocery sales tax to give relief to all Tennesseans' — which would reduce food costs for all families. The platform does not address federal nutrition assistance programs specifically.

parental_support.summary: Fritts supports parental rights in education, including homeschooling and private schooling, but draws the line at taxpayer funding for private schools. His campaign emphasizes parental primacy in children's education and a pro-life stance. No positions on paid family leave, childcare subsidies, or family economic support were found.
parental_support.details: According to TNFirefly, Fritts 'Supports (with limits)' parental rights: he 'supports right of parents to homeschool or send children to private school, but draws the line at taxpayer funding for private schools.' His campaign platform states 'Parents are the first and final voice in their children's education' and lists 'Protecting Innocent Life' as a platform plank: 'Every life is sacred, from conception forward. Defend the unborn with the full authority of the state. Support mothers, fathers, and families who choose life.' No positions on paid family leave, childcare subsidies, the Child Tax Credit, or maternal health programs were found in his campaign materials.

name: Lauren Pinkston
bio: Independent gubernatorial candidate. Former Lipscomb University professor with a detailed family-economic platform — only candidate proposing redirecting Education Freedom Scholarship funds to early childhood ed and employer on-site daycare.
photo_credit: Direct headshot URL not found; visit campaign site

early_childhood_ed.summary: Lauren Pinkston strongly supports redirecting Tennessee's Education Freedom Scholarship funds toward early childhood education and on-site daycare. She frames early childhood investment as an economic growth strategy that enables dual-income households.
early_childhood_ed.details: Pinkston's campaign platform states: 'Lauren strongly supports shifting Tennessee increased budget Education Freedom Scholarships to early childhood education funds, as well as any budget measures that will expand the number of affordable early childhood education opportunities for families in Tennessee. These funds will support businesses that offer on-site daycare, while the state's investment will increase the workforce, expand the economy with dual-income households, and relieve financial pressure on growing families with young children.' As a former elementary school teacher and Ph.D. holder in International Family and Community Studies, she also supports 'limited screens in schools' for younger children, citing research on childhood development. She has discussed the childcare crisis prominently in media appearances.

child_hunger.summary: Pinkston supports reinstating Tennessee's Summer EBT program to connect SNAP families with local farmers; she opposes SNAP food restrictions, supports eliminating the grocery tax, and proposes restructuring public assistance programs to eliminate 'benefit cliffs.'
child_hunger.details: Pinkston's campaign platform states directly: 'Lauren supports reinstating summer EBT funding to connect SNAP families with Tennessee farmers, while helping parents learn how to prepare fresh, local food affordably during the summer months. She will also support incentivizing participation in nutrition classes with additional SNAP funds.' On SNAP restrictions, she 'opposes restrictions that would block SNAP benefits from being used for certain foods like snacks or sodas. These restrictions would harm local grocers and drive up food costs for middle-class families.' She supports eliminating the 4% grocery tax in Tennessee and proposes restructuring public assistance programs to 'eliminate benefit cliffs.' During a February 2026 campaign stop in McKenzie, she cited frustration with barriers to accessing SNAP resources.

parental_support.summary: Pinkston's family-economic platform includes addressing maternity care deserts, supporting access to IVF and contraception, expanding childcare through business incentives, and protecting workers' rights to organize. She proposes eliminating 'benefit cliffs' in public assistance programs.
parental_support.details: Pinkston's platform addresses maternal health directly: 'Over a third of Tennessee counties are considered maternity care deserts and this crisis disproportionately impacts rural, low-income, and Black Tennesseans. Lauren will address maternity care deserts as a public health priority, paying particular attention to dismantling racialized maternity mortality inequities in our state.' She supports full access to reproductive healthcare including IVF and will 'veto any legislation that restricts women's access to contraceptives.' Her childcare policy redirects EFS funds toward on-site daycare to support dual-income households. She proposes restructuring public assistance programs to eliminate 'benefit cliffs' that discourage recipients from increasing their income.

name: Jerri Green
bio: Democratic primary frontrunner running a coalition campaign rooted in West Tennessee. Focused on healthcare, education, and rural-urban balance.
photo_credit: Green for Governor official campaign website

early_childhood_ed.summary: Jerri Green has one of the most detailed early childhood education platforms in the race. She pledges universal pre-K for all Tennessee children, a dedicated childcare and early education fund, and will use $50 million in TANF funds to clear the childcare waitlist on day one.
early_childhood_ed.details: Green's platform includes: 'Invest in universal pre-K, special education, and rural schools' and 'Start a dedicated childcare and early education fund, to include investments in afterschool and summer care programming for households making less than $75K a year.' Her Day One Plan includes: 'Childcare for All: Use $50 Million of TANF funding to clear the waitlist for every family, ensuring no parent has to choose between a paycheck and their child.' She stated one of her two measurable first-term goals is 'using those same [TANF] funds to clear the child care waiting list and help families get into child care that's more affordable and sustainable for the communities as well.' She supports suspending the voucher program to redirect funding to public schools. In a Kingsport town hall (February 2026), she stated: 'We can create subsidies for people who are below the poverty level to help get them quality, affordable childcare.'

child_hunger.summary: Green pledges to protect SNAP from cuts and budget to restore SNAP benefits for Tennesseans affected by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. She has stated that '1 in 5 kids right now in the state of Tennessee goes to bed hungry' and named this as a policy priority.
child_hunger.details: At a February 2026 town hall in Kingsport, Green stated she 'would budget to fund those in need of SNAP/EBT benefits who were affected by the Big Beautiful Bill' and said: '1 in 5 kids right now in the state of Tennessee goes to bed hungry; our governor and government won't step up, and we can change that.' Her platform states she will 'Lift families out of poverty — not punish them with cruel cuts to SNAP or housing aid.' She supports ending the grocery tax by closing corporate tax loopholes. She also committed to incentivizing companies that offer childcare and other worker benefits.

parental_support.summary: Green's platform is the most detailed among all candidates on parental and family support. She supports expanding paid family and medical leave, making childcare affordable, home visiting programs, a diaper stipend for low-income parents, eliminating the tax on diapers, and TANF-funded housing assistance.
parental_support.details: Green's campaign platform states she will 'Make child care affordable and accessible,' 'Expand home visiting programs and early childhood development support,' 'Provide paid leave to parents and caregivers,' 'Lift families out of poverty — not punish them with cruel cuts to SNAP or housing aid,' 'Create a stipend program to offer free diapers to low-income parents,' and 'End the tax on diapers and menstrual products.' Her Day One Plan includes using $10 million in TANF funds to waive security deposits for housing for 100,000+ Tennessee families. She supports 'Expand paid family and medical leave' and labor rights. When announcing her candidacy in July 2025, she stated: 'I want to be able to be the person that makes sure we have paid family leave so more mothers can see their child's first smile.'

name: Dr. Carnita Atwater
bio: Memphis community advocate making her second gubernatorial run. Known for community development work in the New Chicago neighborhood.

early_childhood_ed.summary: Dr. Carnita Atwater has a detailed Universal Pre-K policy platform, proposing a statewide 'Pre-K for All' program funded with $35 million in TANF funds that would provide free, high-quality, voluntary pre-kindergarten to all 3- and 4-year-olds in Tennessee regardless of family income.
early_childhood_ed.details: Atwater's campaign website (atwater4governor.com) includes a dedicated 'Universal Pre-K' policy page stating: 'As the next Governor of the State of Tennessee, I will implement a statewide Pre-K for All agenda. Pre-K for All in Memphis and Shelby County is an initiative providing free, high-quality, voluntary pre-kindergarten to all three and four-year-olds regardless of family income, administered by First 8 Memphis.' She proposes using $35 million from TANF funds to support the program with wraparound housing stability services, targeting all 3- and 4-year-olds statewide, with special emphasis on the poorest distressed counties — Hancock, Grundy, and Lake. She states: 'Widely available early care and education can be a strong economic foundation for families and communities.'

child_hunger.summary: Atwater's campaign website lists a 'TENN FIRE (Food Insecurities Rescue Emergency) Plan' as a named policy initiative, and her stated 'main priority' is to end hunger and improve health outcomes for vulnerable communities, especially rural counties. She supports eliminating the 4% grocery sales tax.
child_hunger.details: Atwater's campaign website lists a 'TENN FIRE (Food Insecurities Rescue Emergency) Plan' among her policy initiatives. Her BallotReady profile states: 'As the next potential Governor of the State of Tennessee, my main priority is to end hunger and improve health outcomes for vulnerable communities across the State of Tennessee, especially the rural counties that have been neglected for too long.' She supports 'Grocery Tax Relief: Eliminates the 4% sales tax on food and food ingredients for home consumption.' Her broader economic platform pledges: 'No citizen in rural Tennessee should be living in a third-world country without running water, modern electricity, food accessibility, healthcare, mental health counseling, drug counseling, and low, livable wages.'

parental_support.summary: Atwater's platform includes a named 'FATHERHOOD INITIATIVE PROGRAM,' a 'WOMEN OPPORTUNITY MANIFESTING EQUITY NOW' plan, and an 'INFANT MORTALITY RATE PLAN.' She emphasizes improving care for rural mothers and babies, addressing maternal mortality, supporting reproductive rights, and ending housing displacement for Tennessee families.
parental_support.details: Atwater's campaign website lists among its policy initiatives a 'FATHERHOOD INITIATIVE PROGRAM — F.A.T.H.E.R.,' a 'WOMEN OPPORTUNITY MANIFESTING EQUITY NOW (W.O.M.E.N.)' plan, an 'INFANT MORTALITY RATE PLAN (I.N.F.A.N.T.),' and a 'DOMESTIC VIOLENCE — STOP ABUSING WOMEN (SAW)' program. Her BallotReady profile states under healthcare: 'Change the poor trajectory of the quality of care rural mothers and babies are receiving. Health care should be a human right.' On abortion/contraception, she states: 'No woman should be denied accessibility to reproductive rights.' She also lists a 'TENNESSEE COMPREHENSIVE CHILD POVERTY PLAN' and a 'FOSTER CARE RECOVERY and HOPE' program on her website.
